While inflation related to high oil prices remains a concern, recent economic data has investors mostly expecting the Federal Reserve to hold interest rates steady at its September meeting. Traders see a 67% chance the Fed will keep rates unchanged at the September meeting, with a 33% chance of a hike, according to CME's FedWatch.

The University of Michigan's preliminary consumer sentiment survey came in at 51 in August, below expectations of 54.5, according to economists polled by Reuters.
